1  HON'BLE AVNISH SAXENA, J. 
1.

Heard Sri Yatindra Kumar Dubey, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Vinay Kumar Mishra,
Advocate holding the brief on behalf of opposite party no.2 and learned AGA for the State.

2.The instant application under Section 528 B.N.S.S. has been moved with a prayer to quash the entire proceeding of the Sessions Trial No.326 of 2019 (State Vs. Ramchandra and others) arising out of Case Crime No.992 of 2015, under Sections 363, 366 and 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Hata, District Kushinagar.

entities.text: Sessions Trial No.326 of 2019 (State Vs. Ramchandra and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Sri Dubey, learned counsel for the applicants appears and submits that the applicant has married the victim.
The applicant nos. 2 to 5 are relatives of applicant no.1.
The father of victim has lodged the FIR of enticement on 03.07.2015.
The informant passed away on 16.11.2016.
His widow Indrawati Devi did not want to continue with the case, as the victim and applicant no.1 are happily married couple having three children.
The birth certificate of children are already on record.

Hence,
seeks intervention of this Court to quash the charge sheet and proceedings.
4. Learned AGA is present for the State-opposite party no.1 and opposed the prayer for quashing the charge sheet.
5. Sri Vinay Kumar Mishra, Advocate holding the brief appears on behalf of opposite party no.2 filed short counter affidavit.
The same is taken on record.
It is submitted that the applicant no.1 and victim were in love affair and married each other on 06.04.2017.
Further stated that three children are born from the wedlock.
The accused-applicant no.1 and victim are happily and peacefully residing and therefore she does not want to continue with the trial of the case.

5. None appears on behalf of opposite party no.3 & 4.
6.
This Court has taken into consideration the factum of marriage between the applicant no.1 and victim having three children.

5. The Apex Court in another case of Mafat Lal and another Vs. The State of Rajasthan (2022) 6 SCC 589 has quashed the F.I.R. and consequential proceedings of offence U/s 363, 366 I.P.C.
considering the marriage of accused and victim.

entities.text: Mafat Lal and another Vs. The State of Rajasthan (2022) 6 SCC 589
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Even in the cases of POCSO Act, the Apex Court has observed in the case of K. Dhandapani Vs.
State by the Inspector of Police (2022 SCC Online SC 1056) has set aside the conviction and sentence of the accused affirmed by the High Court in the matter of POCSO Act considering that the accused and victim are living happily in their married life and held that "This Court cannot shut its eyes to the ground reality and disturb the happy family life of the appellant and the prosecutrix".
7.
